name: trama
description: See your System as a layered Model of state machines, review Proposals and Drifts, and steer your coding agent from one editor tab.

commands.title: Send to agent (closing the tab sends it too)

trama.agentCommand.markdownDescription: Command that starts your coding agent in a terminal. `{prompt}` is replaced by the shell-quoted prompt; if it is missing, the prompt is appended. Examples: `claude {prompt}`, `codex {prompt}`. Trama never calls a model itself.

enumDescriptions: The chat in Cursor, the integrated terminal in every other editor. In Cursor `#trama.agentCommand#` is not needed. Never the external terminal.
Run `#trama.agentCommand#` in the editor's integrated terminal (omp, claude, codex, copilot CLI, Cursor's `agent`…).
Run `#trama.agentCommand#` in the editor's integrated terminal, opened as an editor tab beside the active one.
Run `#trama.agentCommand#` in a window of your system's default terminal, outside the editor (Linux and macOS only, and only for a project opened locally).

Send the prompt to the agent chat built into the editor. In Cursor a new chat sends it by itself; if Cursor does not allow that, the chat waits for your confirmation and Enter, or the prompt is copied to the clipboard. In VS Code it goes to Copilot's chat, or to the clipboard if the chat is not available.
trama.agentLauncher.markdownDescription: Where the Design, Scan and Run buttons send their prompt. `auto` (the default) uses the chat in Cursor and the integrated terminal elsewhere; `terminal` is the editor's integrated terminal; `terminal-tab` is the editor's integrated terminal, opened as an editor tab beside the active one; `external-terminal` is a window of your system's default terminal, outside the editor (Linux and macOS only); `chat` is the agent chat built into the editor. Choosing `terminal`, `terminal-tab`, `external-terminal` or `chat` always wins.

trama.externalTerminalCommand.markdownDescription: Command that opens the external terminal when `#trama.agentLauncher#` is `external-terminal`, instead of the detected one. `{command}` is replaced by the agent's command line, which is appended if `{command}` is missing; for example `alacritty -e {command}`. Empty (the default) detects your system's terminal. With a value set, every instruction opens a new window. It only applies in your user settings.

trama.autoScan.markdownDescription: After you approve a Proposal, launch the agent to Scan the Features it touched. With a terminal launcher (integrated or external) it only applies when `#trama.agentCommand#` is set.

trama.skillsDir.markdownDescription: Folder, relative to the project root, where **Trama: Initialize Project** installs the agent skills. Use `.claude/skills` for Claude Code.

trama.language.markdownDescription: Language the agent writes in, for example `Italian` or `Deutsch`. When set, every instruction Trama sends to the agent asks it to write everything it generates in that language, except code, which always stays in English. Empty (the default) asks nothing about language. It only reaches agents that Trama starts, changes nothing already written, and the Trama interface stays in English.

trama.worktreeAgent.markdownDescription: Command of the worktree terminals, only in your user settings. `{prompt}` is replaced by the shell-quoted prompt; if it is missing, the prompt is appended. Empty prevents turning the multi-branch switch on, and blocks accepting a Proposal while the switch is on.

trama.ntfy.markdownDescription: Name (for example `my-trama-alerts`) or full URL of an [ntfy](https://ntfy.sh) topic. When set, Trama sends a notification when an agent question goes unanswered for 10 seconds and when the agent command ends (in Cursor's chat, when the agent ends its turn) without another instruction starting within 10 seconds. It only covers agents that Trama starts in a terminal and Trama's conversations in Cursor's chat, not the chat of other editors or an agent you start yourself. Empty (the default) sends nothing. It only applies in your user settings. On the public service `https://ntfy.sh` anyone who knows the topic can read the notifications, which contain questions and Board counts, so use a long, hard-to-guess topic or your own server.
